title: Data Structures & Algorithms Certification
description: Assess your understanding of time complexity, arrays, trees, graphs, and dynamic programming.

questions.question: What is the average time complexity of searching in a Balanced Binary Search Tree (AVL Tree)?
questions.explanation: Searching in a balanced BST splits the search space in half at each step, yielding O(log n).

questions.question: Which data structure follows the Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) principle?
questions.explanation: A Stack works on the LIFO principle where elements are pushed and popped from top.

questions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of QuickSort?
questions.explanation: When an unbalanced pivot is picked repeatedly, QuickSort degrades to O(n^2).

questions.question: Which algorithm is commonly used to find the shortest path in a graph with non-negative edge weights?
questions.explanation: Dijkstra's algorithm is optimal for single-source shortest paths on non-negative graphs.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an in-place sorting algorithm?
questions.explanation: Standard Merge Sort requires O(n) auxiliary space to merge subarrays.

title: Modern JavaScript & Web Development Assessment
description: Evaluate modern ES6+ syntax, asynchronous programming, DOM manipulation, and promises.

questions.question: Which keyword is used to declare a block-scoped variable that cannot be reassigned?
questions.explanation: 'const' creates immutable bindings within block scope.

questions.question: What does Promise.all() return if any of the passed promises reject?
options: A promise that immediately rejects with that reason
It waits for all promises to resolve
questions.explanation: Promise.all() rejects immediately as soon as any promise in the iterable rejects.

questions.question: What will `typeof NaN` evaluate to in JavaScript?
questions.explanation: According to the IEEE 754 floating-point standard, NaN is technically a numerical value.

questions.question: Which method turns a JavaScript object into a JSON formatted string?
questions.explanation: JSON.stringify() converts a JavaScript value to a JSON string.

title: SQL & Relational Database Architecture
description: Deep dive into ACID properties, query optimization, indexing strategies, and normalization.

questions.question: Which normal form removes partial functional dependencies on a composite primary key?
questions.explanation: 2NF requires 1NF and no non-prime attribute to be dependent on any proper subset of any candidate key.

questions.question: What does the 'I' in ACID transaction properties stand for?
questions.explanation: Isolation ensures concurrent transactions execute without interfering with one another.

questions.question: Which SQL clause is used to filter records after aggregation with GROUP BY?
questions.explanation: HAVING filters groups created by the GROUP BY clause.

questions.question: Which index structure is most commonly utilized by relational database storage engines for range queries?
questions.explanation: B+ Trees store sequential pointers across leaf nodes, making range queries exceptionally fast.
